Endurance Planner

Seirios Solutions, LLC
Where can an endurance limited deepwater vessel map economically? Live GEBCO and NOAA NCEI layers show what is already measured and where the gaps are. The red line is the efficiency limit for out and back deployments: beyond it, transit eats more of the deployment than your minimum allows. The white line, when turned on, is the US EEZ from Marine Regions. Draw a survey area to get a deployment estimate. All shading applies to ocean only.

Vessel

Efficiency

Efficiency = days on station divided by deployment length. Days on station = deployment minus total transit minus margin. Reach assumes returning to the nearest port, which is always the cheapest option.
Red wash = reachable but below your minimum. Near black = out of reach at all. Land is never shaded.
Cyan = water within the efficiency limit where the budget also covers entering from one port and exiting to a different port, so a deployment can map and finish repositioned instead of returning to where it started.
Rings mark total out and back transit days, one ring per day, colored cyan to violet, drawn over water only.

Survey production

How to plan a survey here
  1. Get an area on the globe. Press Draw area and click at least three points, or press Import GeoJSON to load a footprint or polygon from a file.
  2. Choose how swath is worked out. From depth (sonar curve) is the realistic setting: it takes the swath from the selected sonar at the actual water depth under the polygon. Manual swath holds one width everywhere and will misprice any survey where depth varies.
  3. Set overlap, speed and the rotation. Overlap and survey speed drive the line plan; deployment length, port turnaround and weather margin drive the calendar.
  4. Read the survey report, then Export report for a document, or Send to Cost Model to price it. For a footprint with several areas, add each one to the campaign to total them.
What does overlap mean?
Overlap is the pairwise overlap between adjacent lines: line spacing = swath × (1 − overlap). NOAA-style 20% overlap is entered as 20 here, never doubled for having a neighbor on each side; each shared strip is the full overlap percentage, counted once per line pair. The Cost Model's depth sweep uses the identical convention.
Overlap between adjacent lines sets line spacing = swath × (1 − overlap). Depth mode uses achievable swath angle versus depth curves digitized from the Kongsberg runtime graphs and calibrated to operator data tips (EM124 2°×2° and EM304 MKII 1°×2°; the steps near 9,000 m and 4,200 m are pulse mode changes), with swath = 2 × depth × tan(angle), capped by Max angle. Depth source chooses between the embedded ETOPO bathymetry inside your polygon (the default; spacing computed per depth band) and a static average you set. The survey report plans parallel lines along the polygon's long axis at that spacing and adds one line turn between lines. Port turnaround is the time alongside between deployments; it counts toward calendar time in the survey report.

Layers

GEBCO type identifier grid: lit seafloor has measured bathymetry, dark ocean is interpolated only. These are the gaps. Land always stays at full brightness.

Shows the US EEZ boundary line from the Marine Regions EEZ v12 dataset (low resolution, simplified), including US claimed overlapping areas such as Wake. US EEZ statistics are always shown below the globe. For planning, not legal use.
Basemap: GEBCO shaded relief loading
Layers stream from gebco.net and gis.ngdc.noaa.gov, so this tool needs an internet connection. If a badge shows failed, click it to retry.

Ports included

Reach is computed from every checked port clearing a 2.5 m draft plus 0.5 m under keel. Uncheck groups to test scenarios, for example US only.
Tier 1 = primary support hubs. Tier 2 (marked T2) = smaller or regional ports with workable but limited services, anchorage fueling, or permit requirements. Verify logistics before relying on one.
Custom ports appear at the top of the list below, join the reach model immediately, and are remembered in this browser when possible. Use them for known options, for example the three NOAA piers you are choosing between.
Port depths are AI recalled planning estimates typed into this tool, not pulled from any dataset, and carry no per port citation. They range from well established (major hubs) to judgment calls (small anchorages) and can be stale. Fine for coarse filtering at shallow draft; verify against current sailing directions before any depth actually matters, and use Add your own port to encode verified numbers.

Survey report

Use Draw area, click at least three points on the globe, then press Finish, double click, or right click. You get area, transit, days on station, coverage rate, and how many deployments the polygon costs.

Site check

Click a point on the globe to rank the nearest included ports by transit time and remaining mapping days.
Seirios Solutions internal planning tool, not for distribution. EM124 and EM304 MKII swath curves digitized from Kongsberg runtime coverage graphs; achievable coverage varies with conditions and settings.
Basemap and mapped coverage: imagery reproduced from the GEBCO Grid, www.gebco.net. Multibeam mosaic and bathymetric gap analysis: NOAA NCEI. Embedded depth grid: ETOPO 2022 bedrock (NOAA NCEI), decimated.
Distances are great circle with no routing around land, and polar reach ignores sea ice and seasonal access. US EEZ boundaries: Marine Regions EEZ v12, Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ), simplified; not for legal use. Everything else happens locally in this tab.
Remember these tools were built using AI. Always check outputs against trusted tools before relying on them.
